description: The permission set the main window runs under, audited against what the interface actually calls. The frontend imports three things from @tauri-apps/api: invoke (hayat/jisr.ts), listen (shashat/luba.tsx, shashat/warsha.tsx) and getCurrentWindow (hayat/nafidha.ts). listen is one of two core modules the interface drives, and the unlisten half is used, so core:event:allow-listen and core:event:allow-unlisten are named here even though core:default already implies them; naming them is the record of who consumes them. The other is the window: on Windows the product declines the platform frame (tauri.windows.conf.json sets decorations false) and draws its own strip, so it holds exactly the six window grants that strip needs — start-dragging and internal-toggle-maximize for the drag region Tauri's own script drives from data-tauri-drag-region, minimize, toggle-maximize and close for the three controls, and is-maximized so the middle control shows the right glyph after onResized. Nothing else about the window is granted: no set-title, no set-size, no position, no always-on-top. Progress events are emitted from Rust through tauri::Emitter, never from the webview, so no emit grant is held either. The build's version and name reach the interface through the maalumat_taarib command, not core:app. core:webview:allow-internal-toggle-devtools is retained because it cannot be withdrawn from here: it is a member of core:webview:default and therefore of core:default, and a Capability at tauri 2.11.5 has no debug-only or profile field to scope it with — only platforms, whose values are operating systems. The real gate is the tauri devtools cargo feature; see docs/tawzee/adhonat.md. Nothing here grants filesystem, shell or network access. Those go through Taarib's own commands, which are not governed by this file at all and are validated against taarib_usus::masarat before they touch the machine.
